The unit circle

Drag a point around the circle and watch sin, cos and tan change. Learn the 16 exact values, then drill them until you recognise them instantly.

0 / 10 problems mastered

Every point on the unit circle (radius 1) is (cos⁡θ, sin⁡θ)(\cos\theta,\ \sin\theta)(cosθ, sinθ). cos is the x-coordinate, sin is the y-coordinate. Grab the black point and drag it, tap any angle, or press ▶ Spin. The coloured lines are the actual lengths: blue = cos, pink = sin, orange = tan (tick “Show tan”).

How to memorize it in 5 minutes

1 · Quadrant I is the whole circle

Learn only 0, π6, π4, π3, π20,\ \frac\pi6,\ \frac\pi4,\ \frac\pi3,\ \frac\pi20, 6π​, 4π​, 3π​, 2π​. The other 12 angles reuse these values with a sign.

2 · The √ pattern for sin

sin⁡\sinsin at 0,π6,π4,π3,π20,\frac\pi6,\frac\pi4,\frac\pi3,\frac\pi20,6π​,4π​,3π​,2π​ is

02, 12, 22, 32, 42\tfrac{\sqrt0}{2},\ \tfrac{\sqrt1}{2},\ \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2},\ \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},\ \tfrac{\sqrt4}{2}20​​, 21​​, 22​​, 23​​, 24​​

= 0, 12, 22, 32, 10,\ \tfrac12,\ \tfrac{\sqrt2}2,\ \tfrac{\sqrt3}2,\ 10, 21​, 22​​, 23​​, 1. Count 0-1-2-3-4 under the root.

3 · cos is the same list backwards

cos⁡\coscos: 1, 32, 22, 12, 01,\ \tfrac{\sqrt3}2,\ \tfrac{\sqrt2}2,\ \tfrac12,\ 01, 23​​, 22​​, 21​, 0.

At π6\frac\pi66π​ the point is wide and low, so cos is big and sin is small. At π3\frac\pi33π​ it's the other way round.

4 · tan = sin ÷ cos

tan⁡π6=33\tan\frac\pi6=\tfrac{\sqrt3}3tan6π​=33​​, tan⁡π4=1\tan\frac\pi4=1tan4π​=1, tan⁡π3=3\tan\frac\pi3=\sqrt3tan3π​=3​. tan⁡π2\tan\frac\pi2tan2π​ is undefined (cos = 0).

5 · Other quadrants: reference angle + sign

The reference angle is the angle to the nearest x-axis. Same reference angle means the same numbers; only the signs change.

5π6, 7π6, 11π6\frac{5\pi}6,\ \frac{7\pi}6,\ \frac{11\pi}665π​, 67π​, 611π​ all have reference angle π6\frac\pi66π​.

6 · Signs: All Students Take Calculus

Quadrant I: All positive · II: Sin positive · III: Tan positive · IV: Cos positive.

Or just think: x is negative on the left, y is negative at the bottom.

Recognise the denominators

Denominator 6 → reference π6\frac\pi66π​ · 4 → π4\frac\pi44π​ · 3 → π3\frac\pi33π​. Then the numerator tells you the quadrant: 5π6\frac{5\pi}{6}65π​ is just short of π\piπ (QII), 7π6\frac{7\pi}{6}67π​ just past π\piπ (QIII), 11π6\frac{11\pi}{6}611π​ just short of 2π2\pi2π (QIV).

Degrees ↔ radians

π=180∘\pi=180^\circπ=180∘. Multiply by π180\frac{\pi}{180}180π​ to get radians, or by 180π\frac{180}{\pi}π180​ to get degrees. π6=30∘, π4=45∘, π3=60∘\frac\pi6=30^\circ,\ \frac\pi4=45^\circ,\ \frac\pi3=60^\circ6π​=30∘, 4π​=45∘, 3π​=60∘.

Negative and big angles

−θ-\theta−θ goes clockwise: cos⁡(−θ)=cos⁡θ\cos(-\theta)=\cos\thetacos(−θ)=cosθ, sin⁡(−θ)=−sin⁡θ\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\thetasin(−θ)=−sinθ. For angles past 2π2\pi2π, subtract 2π2\pi2π until you're back in [0,2π)[0,2\pi)[0,2π).

Reciprocals

sec⁡=1cos⁡\sec=\frac1{\cos}sec=cos1​, csc⁡=1sin⁡\csc=\frac1{\sin}csc=sin1​, cot⁡=cos⁡sin⁡\cot=\frac{\cos}{\sin}cot=sincos​. Find cos or sin first, then flip it.

Where it shows up in calculus

  • Critical numbers with trig (§4.1, §4.3): solving cos⁡x=12\cos x=\tfrac12cosx=21​ means reading the circle backwards: x=π3,5π3x=\frac\pi3,\frac{5\pi}3x=3π​,35π​.
  • Inverse trig (§3.6): sin⁡−1\sin^{-1}sin−1 and tan⁡−1\tan^{-1}tan−1 give angles in [−π2,π2][-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2][−2π​,2π​] (the right half), and cos⁡−1\cos^{-1}cos−1 gives angles in [0,π][0,\pi][0,π] (the top half).
  • Evaluating derivatives: f′(π4)f'(\frac\pi4)f′(4π​) for f=tan⁡xf=\tan xf=tanx is sec⁡2π4=(2)2=2\sec^2\frac\pi4=(\sqrt2)^2=2sec24π​=(2​)2=2.
  • l'Hospital and limits (§4.4): you need cos⁡0=1\cos0=1cos0=1, sin⁡0=0\sin0=0sin0=0 and cos⁡π=−1\cos\pi=-1cosπ=−1 instantly.

Traps

Swapping sin and cos

The point is (cos⁡,sin⁡)(\cos,\sin)(cos,sin), x first, like the alphabet: c before s.

Wrong sign

Always ask which quadrant before writing the number. Left half: cos is negative. Bottom half: sin is negative.

Calculator in degrees

sin⁡(π/6)\sin(\pi/6)sin(π/6) in degrees mode gives 0.0091, not 0.5. Calculus uses radians.

Inverse trig giving the wrong angle

sin⁡−1(−12)\sin^{-1}(-\frac12)sin−1(−21​) is −π6-\frac\pi6−6π​, not 7π6\frac{7\pi}667π​ or 11π6\frac{11\pi}6611π​: it must be in [−π2,π2][-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2][−2π​,2π​].
